chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who inherited a slave jointly, and one of them freed his share from him. What is to be done regarding the one who freed his share? Is the remainder taken [from him]? He said: 'The remainder is taken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one partner frees their share of a jointly owned slave?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of partial manumission (*'itq ba'id*), establishing that the freed share absorbs the remaining obligation, thereby reducing the slave's status proportionally. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that manumission is a divisible right among co-owners, ensuring the slave's gradual liberation without requiring the consent of other partners for the specific share being freed.
